label: Laurence J. Kotlikoff
narrative: Laurence Kotlikoff is a Professor of Economics at Boston University known for work on generational accounting and fiscal transparency. He co-wrote three Forbes columns with Mark Skidmore about the unsupported adjustment aggregate: 'Has Our Government Spent $21 Trillion of Our Money without Telling Us?' in December 2017, 'Is Our Government Intentionally Hiding $21 Trillion in Spending?' in July 2018, and 'Holding U.S. Treasurys? Beware: Uncle Sam Can't Account for $21 Trillion' in January 2019. His role matters chiefly for the framing of the second and third pieces: an economist whose career has been spent arguing that the federal government's published fiscal accounts systematically understate obligations arrived independently at the view that the unsupported-adjustment record raised a question about the integrity of the accounts as a whole, and put that view in front of holders of Treasury securities. The July 2018 column's headline question - whether the concealment was intentional - was published nine months after the Department of Defense had, in August 2016, asked FASAB for the standard that became SFFAS 56, and three months before that standard issued.
